original_question: Let V_T be the Frobenius variety of numerical semigroups admitting a Toms decomposition. Determine whether V_T is the least Frobenius variety containing all numerical semigroups of embedding dimension 2.
target_in_paper: Section 4, page 19: the explicit open question asking whether the Frobenius variety of numerical semigroups admitting a Toms decomposition is the least Frobenius variety containing all numerical semigroups of embedding dimension two.
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper's exact question. It correctly identifies the relevant class (numerical semigroups admitting a Toms decomposition), the ambient notion (Frobenius variety), and the precise minimality question relative to all embedding-dimension-two numerical semigroups. The only real gap is that your notation V_T is not from the paper and the paper's nearby context makes several definitions explicit that your draft leaves implicit.
missing_details: The paper does not use the notation V_T; this notation should be introduced explicitly if retained.
A numerical semigroup should be identified as a cofinite additive submonoid of N containing 0.
Embedding dimension 2 means that the minimal system of generators of the numerical semigroup has cardinality 2.

A Toms decomposition must be defined: S admits one if there exist n >= 1 and positive integers q1,...,qn,m1,...,mn,L such that gcd(qi,mi)=gcd(L,qi)=gcd(L,mi)=1 for every i and S = intersection over i of (<qi,mi>/L).
The quotient notation <qi,mi>/L should be defined as {x in N : Lx belongs to <qi,mi>}.

A Frobenius variety should be defined as a nonempty family V of numerical semigroups such that if S,T are in V, then S intersect T is in V, and if S is in V with S not equal to N, then S union {F(S)} is in V.

The phrase 'least Frobenius variety containing all semigroups with embedding dimension two' should be made precise as the intersection of all Frobenius varieties containing that family, i.e. the Frobenius variety generated by the family of embedding-dimension-two numerical semigroups.

The nearby context also records two facts that motivate the question and should be remembered when making it stand-alone: the class of Toms-decomposable numerical semigroups is itself a Frobenius variety, and every embedding-dimension-two numerical semigroup admits a Toms decomposition.
refined_question: Let VT be the family of numerical semigroups S subseteq N (that is, cofinite additive submonoids of N containing 0) that admit a Toms decomposition: there exist n >= 1 and positive integers q1,...,qn,m1,...,mn,L such that gcd(qi,mi)=gcd(L,qi)=gcd(L,mi)=1 for every i and S = intersection_{i=1}^n (<qi,mi>/L), where <qi,mi>/L := {x in N : Lx is in the numerical semigroup generated by qi and mi}. A Frobenius variety is a nonempty family V of numerical semigroups such that (i) S,T in V implies S intersect T in V, and (ii) if S in V and S is not equal to N, then S union {F(S)} is in V, where F(S) is the Frobenius number of S. Since VT is a Frobenius variety and every numerical semigroup of embedding dimension 2 belongs to VT, is VT exactly the Frobenius variety generated by all embedding-dimension-two numerical semigroups; equivalently, is VT the least Frobenius variety containing every numerical semigroup whose minimal system of generators has cardinality 2?
equivalent_formulation: Using the equivalence proved nearby in the paper, the same question can be stated as follows: is the Frobenius variety of numerical semigroups that are finite intersections of proportionally modular numerical semigroups equal to the Frobenius variety generated by all embedding-dimension-two numerical semigroups?
justification: This draft matches a specific open question stated in Section 4, not a broader neighboring problem. Section 4 first defines Frobenius varieties, then notes that numerical semigroups admitting a Toms decomposition form a Frobenius variety and that every embedding-dimension-two numerical semigroup admits a Toms decomposition, and then asks essentially your question verbatim. To make the question fully stand-alone, one must import from Section 3 the exact definition of a Toms decomposition and the equivalent characterization as a finite intersection of proportionally modular numerical semigroups, and from Section 4 the precise meaning of 'least Frobenius variety' as the Frobenius variety generated by a family. The refined version stays exactly at that scope and does not broaden to other varieties or quotient problems.
